task: Distinguish simulated proton-proton collision events in which a Higgs boson is produced (signal) from background events.
instructions: You are helping a feature-selection search for a classification task. Rate how useful each feature is likely to be for predicting the class, on its own or together with a few others, from 0 (useless) to 1 (most useful). Use only your knowledge of the domain and the descriptions given; you do not see the data. Reply with a JSON object only: {"scores": {"<feature index>": <score>, ...}} with one entry for every feature index listed.

calls.reply:
This looks like the HIGGS dataset from UCI (Baldi et al.), but the feature names are anonymized, so I'm relying on my memory of its standard column order.

Assumed layout:
- 0: lepton pT
- 1: lepton eta
- 2: lepton phi
- 3: missing energy magnitude
- 4: missing energy phi
- 5: jet 1 pt
- 6: jet 1 eta
- 7: jet 1 phi
- 8: jet 1 b-tag
- 9: jet 2 pt
- 10: jet 2 eta
- 11: jet 2 phi
- 12: jet 2 b-tag
- 13: jet 3 pt
- 14: jet 3 eta
- 15: jet 3 phi
- 16: jet 3 b-tag
- 17: jet 4 pt
- 18: jet 4 eta
- 19: jet 4 phi
- 20: jet 4 b-tag
- 21: m_jj
- 22: m_jjj
- 23: m_lv
- 24: m_jlv
- 25: m_bb
- 26: m_wbb
- 27: m_wwbb

The 21 low-level features are the first 21 columns, and the 7 high-level mass features are the last 7. The high-level masses are the most discriminating, especially m_bb (25), m_wbb (26) and m_wwbb (27). Among the low-level features, the jet pTs and lepton pT carry some signal. The angular features (phi, eta) are mostly uninformative on their own.

Scores follow that ordering: highest for 25, 26 and 27, then the other masses, then the pT and b-tag features, then the angular ones.
